title.en: List the five steps of the controlling process
Explain setting standards, measuring and comparing

say.en: A cricket coach sets a target of 20 runs per over, counts the runs actually scored and compares. Business control starts the same way. In this lesson: List the five steps of the controlling process.
Explain setting standards, measuring and comparing.
Compute deviation as a percentage.

body.en: The controlling process has five *steps*: setting performance standards, measuring actual performance, comparing actual performance with standards, analysing deviations, and taking corrective action.
body.kn: ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆಯ ಐದು ಹಂತಗಳು: ಮಾನದಂಡ ನಿಗದಿ, ವಾಸ್ತವ ಸಾಧನೆಯ ಮಾಪನ, ಹೋಲಿಕೆ, ವಿಚಲನೆಗಳ ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ತಿದ್ದುಪಡಿ ಕ್ರಮ.

explanation.en: Set standards, measure, compare, analyse deviations, then correct: the five steps of controlling.

steps.en: Set the standard: 10,000 packets a day
Measure actual output: 9,200 packets were made
Compare: the deviation is 800 packets, 8% below standard
Analyse the deviation: it is significant; the cause is a faulty oven
Take corrective action: repair the oven and recheck output

body.en: *Standards* are the criteria against which performance is measured. They may be quantitative (units produced, cost per unit, sales in rupees) or qualitative (goodwill, motivation). Performance is measured by personal observation, sample checking, performance reports and similar methods, preferably in the same units as the standard. Comparison shows the deviation: $\text{Deviation} = \text{Actual} - \text{Standard}$.
body.kn: ಮಾನದಂಡಗಳು ಸಾಧನೆ ಅಳೆಯುವ ಅಳತೆಗೋಲು: ಸಂಖ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕ ಅಥವಾ ಗುಣಾತ್ಮಕ. ವೀಕ್ಷಣೆ, ಮಾದರಿ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ವರದಿಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸಾಧನೆ ಅಳೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೋಲಿಕೆ ವಿಚಲನೆಯನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: The standard labour cost is ₹200 per unit. The actual labour cost this month is ₹230 per unit. Find the deviation and the percentage deviation.

steps.en: Deviation = Actual − Standard = 230 − 200 = ₹30 per unit (unfavourable, as cost is higher).
This deviation is then analysed in step 4 to see if it is significant.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. The standard labour cost is ₹200 per unit. The actual labour cost this month is ₹230 per unit. Find the deviation and the percentage deviation.

say.en: Let us work through this case together. The standard labour cost is 200 rupees per unit. The actual labour cost this month is 230 rupees per unit. Find the deviation and the percentage deviation.
Deviation equals Actual - Standard equals 230 minus 200 equals 30 rupees per unit (unfavourable, as cost is higher).
Percentage deviation equals 30 divided by 200 times 100 equals 15 percent.
This deviation is then analysed in step 4 to see if it is significant.
So the answer is 30 rupees per unit, i.e. 15 percent above standard unfavourable.
